messages:
sarah.k: Heads-up — CI on main started failing after the poetry lock change merged this morning. Local repro shows an ImportError in the frontend inference worker when importing tokenizers. Full log below.

ci-bot: [job: inference-worker-tests] failed with exit code 1
```
> File ".../env/lib/python3.11/site-packages/tokenizers/__init__.py", line 12, in <module>
>     from .backends import *
> ImportError: cannot import name 'backends' from 'tokenizers'
```

sarah.k: The merged lock bumped starlette to 0.22.x and pulled in a wheel-only tokenizers 0.15.2 that doesn't include our patched C-extension build. I suspect poetry resolved to a prebuilt wheel for linux-x86_64 which breaks our alpine/manylinux CI.

maria: Is this related to the CVE we triaged last week for tokenizers? I thought we pinned a patched line. :thinking:

security-bot: CVE trackers: tokenizers CVE-2025-0412 (parsing DoS) was fixed in >=0.14.8. No known RCE for 0.15.x as of last scan. Starlette had CVE-2025-0222 (path traversal) patched in 0.21.6. The current lock moved to 0.22.0 which is not yet approved by security policy.

raj: Thanks. Two problems then: functional CI break (import/build) and policy — starlette 0.22 is unapproved. We need a mitigation plan that doesn't widen the window.

tim.o: Quick mitigation option: pin tokenizers to our validated wheel build in the constraints file and downgrade starlette back to 0.21.6 in the lock, then run full e2e. I can push a hotfix branch: `hotfix/poetry-lock-pins` and open PR with the locked poetry.lock.

sarah.k: Sounds good. Can we also add an audit tag to the PR for compliance? We need an explicit reviewer from security and a record in audit logs when we change dependency approvals.

maria: Yes — please include `security-approval: required` label and set the PR template section: "Security impact & approval". Also request KMS access audit if this touches any code paths that call the key manager (the inference worker rotates keys at startup). Not sure it does, but flagging it.

raj: Action items: 1) tim.o create hotfix PR that pins tokenizers to `0.15.1+patched` (our internal wheel) and sets starlette==0.21.6 in poetry.lock, 2) run `./dev/ci/build-manylinux-wheel.sh` in the PR to validate the extension presence, 3) security does quick CVE verification and signs off, 4) merge and trigger canary on staging for 1 hour.

tim.o: Creating branch and PR now. Will include command to regenerate the lock without resolving other deps: `poetry lock --no-update && git add poetry.lock && git commit -m "lock: pin tokenizers wheel & starlette rollback (hotfix)"`

ci-bot: started job inference-worker-tests (hotfix/poetry-lock-pins)

security-bot: Note: after merge, update the dependency approval spreadsheet and log entry: `deps-audit.csv` with columns (pkg,version,approved_by,approval_ts,notes). I'll add a row when security signs off.

maria: Also please add a one-line regression test that imports tokenizers in our alpine-based CI image so we catch wheel vs source mismatches next time.

sarah.k: If canary looks good for 1 hour, we backport to release-v1.2 and cut a micro release. Keep me posted. :thumbsup:

raj: I'll coordinate the post-merge audit and confirm the KMS access log path. If anything looks suspicious, we can roll back traffic routing to the fallback model pool.

(15m later)
tim.o: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4721 — includes pinned tokenizers, starlette rollback, CI job tweak. Running e2e now.

ci-bot: e2e: passed on staging-canary at 1870123520

sarah.k: Security acked in PR comment and security-bot updated deps-audit.csv row. Planning merge in 10m after one more passing run.

maria: Good job team. After merge we'll follow-up with a short postmortem note on root cause (poetry resolution picking incompatible wheel) and add a CI guard to fail if lock contains unapproved major versions for web frameworks.

raj: Closing loop: remind infra to publish a pinned manylinux wheel for tokenizers to our internal package index so poetry prefers it over external builds.

sarah.k: Thanks everyone — this felt contained. We'll track the postmortem in #postmortems once written. :white_check_mark:
